Exhibition name: Duchesse d'Auerstädt
rows.Origin:
Discovered by Alexandre Bernaix (France, 1887).
Introduced in Australia by C. F. Newman and Sons - Adelaide in 1894 as 'Duchesse d'Auerstaedt'.
rows.Bloom: Golden-yellow, lighter shading. Moderate fragrance. up to 35 petals. Average diameter 5". Large, very double, borne mostly solitary, cupped, scalloped bloom form. Blooms in flushes throughout the season.
rows.Habit:
Medium, climbing. Large, glossy foliage.

Height: 10' to 20' (305 to 610cm). Width: 6' (185cm).
rows.Growing: USDA zone 7b through 10b. Disease susceptibility: very disease resistant.
